title: Color Standards
slide_intent: Establish a common reference for judging a color across production processes. A large sample gives printers and designers a physical target for comparison.
strategic_value: NASA can give suppliers the same reference for its red and warm gray across media. The two large fields make mismatches easier to inspect.
demonstration: The page places two broad horizontal swatches beneath a short reproduction note. The upper field is NASA red and the lower field is NASA warm gray.
practical_value: Use the historical printed samples as the manual’s matching reference. The digitized page records the guidance but does not establish a calibrated color value.

content_islands.name: Production notes
content_islands.spec: Set the heading and two short explanations above the swatches, including the manual’s process-print guidance.

content_islands.name: Paired swatches
content_islands.spec: Stack two large rectangles of equal width with a white gutter. Place red first and warm gray below it.

reference_purposes.Expression: The two large fields show NASA red and NASA warm gray as the manual’s color specimens.
reference_purposes.Application: The note instructs producers to visually match the printed swatches and gives a four-color-process formula for NASA red.

ingredient.name: NASA color matching swatches
ingredient.role: Supply a common physical target for reproducing the two named colors.
ingredient.application: Use the original printed swatches to achieve a visual match. For four-color printing, the manual states solid red plus solid yellow for NASA red.
ingredient.scope: Historical physical production references in section 1.5. The scanned image records the specimens and formula; its pixels do not establish calibrated modern color values.
